# Social-messenger choreography harness

This directory contains the P2-hardened Playwright harness for Clique's
milestone choreography, extended for M8. It launches isolated Alice and Bob
browser contexts, adds Carol for M5 and a second same-account Alice context for
M8, signs them in through the contract's `sm-auth-*` IDs, runs selected `m1()`
through `m6()` and `m8()` segments, and writes structured JSONL receipts.

The harness consumes only test IDs frozen in `../CONTRACT.md`. A runtime guard
rejects any other ID. It never turns missing automation surface into a pass.

## Setup and usage

The instrument intentionally has no lockfile before P3 freeze. A runner must
provision the pinned Playwright and AJV dependencies from `package.json` and the
selected Playwright browser.

```sh
cd benchmarks/tools/social-messenger/choreography
npm install
npx playwright install chromium

CHOREO_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:5173 \
CHOREO_PASSWORD='fixture-password' \
volta run --node 24.18.0 node choreography.mjs m3 \
  --suite-status /absolute/path/suite-status.json
```

`npm test` starts a tiny calibration app, executes M1 and M8 through the real
multi-context harness, validates every emitted receipt against
`receipts.schema.json`, and requires honest segment greens. The app implements
the M8 likes, multi-device unread, live-message, and warm-offline queue surfaces
instead of short-circuiting browser observations. A second M8 run deliberately
serves stale Insights and must exit non-green. The test also exercises the pure
aggregation edge cases: optional skip, required skip, and implemented failure.

The positional segment argument is optional and defaults to `all`. It accepts
`all`, one milestone (`m1` ... `m6` or `m8`), or a comma-separated ordered
subset such as `m1,m3,m8`. `all` runs M1–M6 followed by M8; M7 remains the
brief's separate fresh-session milestone and has no web choreography segment.

Scoring DAG: M3 requires M1 only; M3 does not require M2. Reduced-run
protocol: execute M1, then M2, then M3 in that order. Do not start M3 to
avoid an unfinished M2. A reduced run that skips M2 is non-conforming even
though M3's scoring prerequisite is only M1.

Every implemented CLI flag is:

- `--browser <chromium|firefox|webkit>` — browser engine; default `chromium`.
- `--headed` — show both browser windows; default is headless.
- `--receipts <path>` — JSONL destination; default is `receipts.jsonl` beside
  `choreography.mjs`. The file is truncated at the beginning of each run.
- `--observations <path>` — typed D0.6 assertion-attempt/wait stream; defaults
  to `<receipts>.observations.jsonl`. The metering manifest hash-binds this
  stream before it projects the choreography-owned browser-wait counts. Each
  attempt records only actual locator, predicate, or page-event settlement
  intervals; setup/action and other attempt wall are excluded.
- `--lane-run-id <id>` — required stable lane identity, shared with the
  metering manifest (`CHOREO_LANE_RUN_ID` is the environment form).
- `--suite-status <path>` — required JSON object keyed by milestone. Every
  selected segment must have `{ "pass": boolean, "receipt": string|null }`.
  The runner validates this complete linkage before credentials, Playwright,
  receipt creation, or browser startup. A passing value must carry a non-empty
  suite evidence pointer in `receipt`. Receipt paths are relative to the
  suite-status file, must remain under its directory, and are statted and
  SHA-256 digested before startup. The digest is retained in the segment
  summary so the meter can detect a change when it writes the record.
- `--adapter <path>` — optional lane navigation/fixture adapter. It carries
  route paths and fixture choices only; it cannot report outcomes or bypass
  browser observations. The built-in adapter uses `/profile/{handle}`,
  `/profile/edit`, `/settings`, `/search`, and `/insights` plus the committed
  fixture pack. `routes.insights` may override the M8 Insights route.
- `--simulator-status <path>` — optional separately recorded M6/M8 simulator
  statuses. A single legacy status object is accepted, as is a bundle keyed by
  `m6` and/or `m8`; entries use `{ "id":"ios-simulator-m6"|
  "ios-simulator-m8", "pass":true|false|null, "receipt":string|null,
  "reason":string|null }`. Each entry is retained only in its matching summary
  and never gates web green; see `simulator.md`.
- `--timeout <ms>` — positive integer timeout for ordinary UI observations;
  default `10000`. The M3 2-second appearance and 5-second expiry ceilings are
  fixed by the brief and are not relaxed by this flag.
- `--help` — print usage without loading Playwright.

Exit code `0` means every selected segment has `green:true` (suite plus complete
required choreography). Exit code `1` means execution completed but at least one
segment was not green because a required check was skipped, an implemented
check failed, or suite evidence was absent/failing. Exit code `2` is
configuration or fatal harness failure.

## Environment variables

- `CHOREO_BASE_URL` — required lane web URL.
- `CHOREO_LANE_RUN_ID` — required stable lane identity unless
  `--lane-run-id` is supplied.
- `CHOREO_PASSWORD` — shared fixture password fallback for Alice, Bob, and Carol;
  Alice's M8 second context uses the same Alice credential.
- `CHOREO_ALICE_PASSWORD`, `CHOREO_BOB_PASSWORD` — per-persona passwords;
  `CHOREO_CAROL_PASSWORD` is also required for M5 unless the shared fallback is
  set. Passwords have no CLI flags so
  they do not appear in the process command line.
- `CHOREO_ALICE_EMAIL`, `CHOREO_BOB_EMAIL`, `CHOREO_CAROL_EMAIL` — optional;
  defaults are the corresponding `@example.com` personas from `CONTRACT.md`.
- `CHOREO_BROWSER` — default for `--browser`.
- `CHOREO_RECEIPTS` — default for `--receipts`.
- `CHOREO_OBSERVATIONS` — default for the typed assertion-wait sidecar.
- `CHOREO_SUITE_STATUS` — default for `--suite-status`.
- `CHOREO_ADAPTER` — default for `--adapter`.
- `CHOREO_SIMULATOR_STATUS` — default for `--simulator-status`.
- `CHOREO_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE` — optional browser executable path for runners
  using a system Chromium/Chrome with the Playwright protocol package.
- `CHOREO_TIMEOUT_MS` — default for `--timeout`.

CLI values override their environment defaults. `--headed` has no environment
alias.

## Segment coverage after P2 hardening

Implemented checks make real UI observations and fail normally
when the lane does not satisfy them:

- M1: display-name/bio edits appear on the other client live; session survives
  reload; logout remains signed out across reload.
- M2: live text-post delivery, follow/unfollow Following projection, author
  display name on `sm-feed-item`, live like/unlike count, repost attribution
  and removal, follow-edge vs viewer-repost disambiguation on Following, and
  reply count/thread projection. Live checks run all three trials.
- M3: live DM text on `sm-convo-bubble`, typing visibility within 2 seconds
  and expiry within 5 seconds, plus quoted excerpt and jump behavior through
  the excerpt-only `sm-convo-quote-preview` selector. Live checks run
  best-of-three.
- M4: photo render, video playback, reaction set/replace/remove, edit visibility,
  and delete-for-everyone tombstones across the isolated Alice/Bob contexts.
- M5: group color/background synchronization to Carol, view-once first/second
  view behavior, warm-offline search, and shortened-window disappearing purge.
- M6 web: two offline messages expose pending state, reconnect, arrive exactly
  in order, and reach read receipts.
- M8 web: Bob's like increments Alice's refreshed Insights total; a second
  Alice context receives a same-account message live; opening the conversation
  on Alice client 1 clears `sm-chats-unread` on client 2; and two warm-offline
  Alice clients each queue a message, reconnect in an observed server-arrival
  order, converge without duplicates, and reach normal read receipts.

Remaining unsupported assertions are emitted as `status:"skipped"`, with
`pass:null`, a reason, and whether they are required. Required skips keep the
segment non-green; optional skips are visible but do not masquerade as failures:

- M2 image/video composition (no compose media-picker test ID).
- M2 feed-author avatar (no feed-avatar test ID; display name is required).
- M3 sender-avatar (no sender-avatar test ID; live DM text is required).
- M3 semantic sent/delivered/read tokens (`sm-convo-receipt` exists, but
  glyph/color inference is not an honest state-machine proof).
- M3 group aggregate-receipt and member-removal/history (no group-member
  lifecycle controls in the frozen contract).

The hardening extends the coordination contract for semantic controls and adds
a frozen route/fixture adapter for the four places where navigation cannot be
inferred from a component test ID. The adapter is input-only; the browser still
performs and observes every check.

## Receipts and green aggregation

Each assertion prints one line beginning `STRUCTURED RECEIPT ` and appends the
raw JSON object to the JSONL file. Timing-sensitive assertions always retain all
three attempts. A per-segment summary follows its assertions.

See `receipts-format.md` for field meanings and `receipts.schema.json` for the
machine schema. Milestone green is fail-closed:

```text
green = suite.pass === true && choreography.pass === true
```

Segment summaries also emit `nonGreenCause` (`null` when green; otherwise
`suite-failed` | `choreography-failed` | `required-unimplemented` |
`instrument`). The field remains optional on the schema since `0.3.1-m8` (default
`null`); the emitter always writes it. Prior `0.3.0-m8` receipts remain
governed by their matching schema revision. Lanes MUST copy that field into
the run record. Do not invent a second green label such as "functionally
green".

M6 and M8 web green are intentionally distinct from their simulator artifacts.
`simulator.md` remains the native proof contract; each matching status is
recorded under `choreography.supplementalExternal` and scored as native/O4
evidence rather than silently making web milestones unreachable.

## 0.3.3-m8 migration

`0.3.3-m8` is the coordinated observability bump for LLP 0295 R2. Runners
MUST pass `--suite-status` (or `CHOREO_SUITE_STATUS`) and the file MUST contain
an entry for every selected segment. Missing or partial linkage exits `2`
before any browser or receipt starts; it is no longer represented as a late
`green:false` instrument result. Run records retain the input and suite
receipts in the additive `socialMessenger.suiteStatusLinkage` block.

The same instrument pin adds additive, hash-linked D0.6 milestone fields for
semantic actions, failure-to-recovery episodes, restart/reseed counts, browser
assertion waits, host load, and API interruptions. The run-record extension
stays at version `2` for old-record compatibility; current records must carry
`instrumentVersion: "social-messenger@0.3.3-m8"` and must carry each block as
either claimed or explicitly non-claimed. Browser waits have independent
`suite` and `choreography` owners: this executable claims only choreography,
while the production lane controller records actual suite settlement waits.
The W2 five-counter
native-usage channel is unchanged, while its meter now verifies and joins the
typed observation sidecars.

`0.3.2-m8` uses the unambiguous `sm-convo-quote-preview` selector as the sole
quoted-excerpt jump path after the Clique kit's matching `0.3.1-m8` migration.
`0.3.1-m8` preferred the preview selector with a reply-bubble-scoped legacy
`sm-convo-quote` fallback for `0.3.0`-era clients.
`0.3.0-m8` added the M8 choreography surfaces.
# Social-messenger choreography receipts

Version `0.3.3-m8` writes newline-delimited JSON to `receipts.jsonl`. The same
objects are written to stdout with the literal prefix `STRUCTURED RECEIPT ` so
an outer run harness can separate proof records from ordinary process output.
Each line validates independently against `receipts.schema.json`.

## Assertion receipts

Every browser check emits one `type: "assertion"` object. Its stable identity
is `(segment, assertion)`. The required proof fields are:

- `segment`: one of `m1` through `m6`, or `m8`.
- `assertion`: the stable choreography assertion name.
- `implemented`: whether this harness version actually attempted the check.
- `required`: whether leaving this assertion unimplemented blocks the segment.
- `status`: `passed`, `failed`, or `skipped`.
- `pass`: boolean for an attempted check and `null` for an explicit skip.
- `timings`: every attempt, including errors and all three timing attempts.
- `bestOf`: `1` for ordinary checks and `3` for timing-sensitive checks.

Every timing has both `durationMs` (complete check-attempt wall) and
`settlementWaitMs` (the union of actual locator, predicate, and page-event
wait intervals during that attempt). The latter excludes setup, browser
actions, and computation, and therefore never exceeds `durationMs`. D0.6
choreography wait observations are derived from `settlementWaitMs`, not from
whole-attempt duration. The suite producer records its own settlement waits in
the production lane-controller stream; choreography does not claim them.

An unsupported check is not omitted and never passes. It has
`implemented:false`, `status:"skipped"`, `pass:null`, an empty `timings` array,
and a non-empty `details.reason`. A required skip blocks choreography green; an
optional skip remains visible without being reported as a failed attempt.

For `bestOf:3`, the harness always runs all three attempts. The assertion passes
when at least one attempt passes, and `details.selectedAttempt` identifies the
fastest passing attempt by total `durationMs`; all attempts remain in the
receipt. Metric-specific durations such as `visibleMs` and `expiresMs` remain
under each attempt's `metrics` object. This is best-of-three flake control, not
permission to discard measurements.

For M3's `quoted-reply-excerpt-and-jump` assertion, each attempt's existing
`timing.note` records the `sm-convo-quote-preview` jump selector.

## Segment summaries and milestone green

After the assertion lines, each selected milestone emits one
`type: "segment-summary"` object. This is the per-segment object consumed by the
outer run harness:

```json
{
  "type": "segment-summary",
  "segment": "m3",
  "assertion": "__segment__",
  "implemented": false,
  "required": true,
  "status": "failed",
  "pass": false,
  "timings": [
    {
      "attempt": 1,
      "pass": false,
      "startedAt": null,
      "durationMs": 18234.5,
      "settlementWaitMs": 18001.2,
      "metrics": {}
    }
  ],
  "bestOf": 1,
  "assertions": {
    "total": 3,
    "required": 3,
    "implemented": 2,
    "passed": 2,
    "failed": 0,
    "skipped": 1,
    "notImplemented": 1,
    "requiredUnimplemented": 1
  },
  "suite": { "pass": true, "receipt": "acceptance/m3.json" },
  "choreography": {
    "browserPass": false,
    "requiredExternal": [],
    "externalPass": true,
    "supplementalExternal": [],
    "pass": false
  },
  "green": false,
  "nonGreenCause": "required-unimplemented"
}
```

The normative aggregation is:

1. `browserPass` is true only when every implemented assertion passes and no
   required assertion remains unimplemented. Optional skips therefore stay
   explicit without becoming silent failed attempts.
2. `externalPass` is true when every external leg required for web green passes.
   In `0.3.3-m8` there are no such legs. M6's `ios-simulator-m6` and M8's
   `ios-simulator-m8` statuses are recorded in their matching summaries under
   `supplementalExternal` with `requiredForGreen:false`; they are distinct
   native/O4 artifacts governed by `simulator.md`.
3. `choreography.pass` (and the summary's top-level `pass`) is
   `browserPass && externalPass === true`.
4. `green` is true only when `suite.pass === true && choreography.pass === true`.
   Version `0.3.3-m8` refuses missing or partial suite-status linkage before
   creating receipts or starting a browser, so emitted `suite.pass` is always
   boolean.
5. `nonGreenCause` is the closed recording convention for a non-green
   segment. It is optional on the schema (default `null` when omitted) so
   existing `0.3.0-m8` receipts remain valid; emitters since `0.3.1-m8`
   always write it. Allowed values:
   - `null` — `green` is true. There is no second green label.
   - `required-unimplemented` — a required assertion was skipped.
   - `choreography-failed` — an implemented assertion failed.
   - `suite-failed` — suite evidence is `pass:false`.
   - `instrument` — non-green for an instrument defect other than missing
     suite linkage, which `0.3.3-m8` refuses before startup.

   Lanes MUST copy `nonGreenCause` from this summary into the run record.
   Do not invent labels such as "functionally green". `green` stays a
   boolean; `capability-failure` remains the brief's cap-exhausted
   milestone status, not a synonym for instrument-caused non-green.

The required suite-status input is an object keyed by milestone. Every selected
milestone must be present:

```json
{
  "m1": { "pass": true, "receipt": "acceptance/m1.json" },
  "m2": { "pass": false, "receipt": "acceptance/m2.json" },
  "m8": { "pass": true, "receipt": "acceptance/m8.json" }
}
```

The path is relative to the suite-status file. The choreography does not
interpret or bless the builder's suite semantics, but it does stat and digest
the actual file before startup. The segment summary retains that SHA-256; the
meter re-stats and re-digests the same file at record-write time. A missing or
changed passing receipt refuses rather than becoming green. Coverage-manifest
validation belongs to the outer run harness described by the benchmark brief.

## Compatibility

Consumers must reject an unknown major receipt version and validate with the
schema matching the declared version; unknown fields are rejected. Stable
`(segment, assertion)` names must not be silently repurposed;
changed semantics require a version bump. `nonGreenCause` is an optional
additive field introduced on `0.3.1-m8` segment summaries (default `null`
when omitted); it did not bump the receipt version. `0.3.2-m8` IS a semantic
bump: it removes the legacy `sm-convo-quote` jump fallback, so an M3
`quoted-reply-excerpt-and-jump` receipt at `0.3.2-m8` proves preview-only
selection, while a `0.3.1-m8` receipt may have recorded the reply-bubble-
scoped fallback.

`0.3.3-m8` keeps `0.3.2-m8` selector semantics and makes suite-status linkage
startup-refusing. It coordinates the additive LLP 0295 D0.6 run-record
observability fields without changing `extensionVersion: 2`; the W2 token
meter now joins typed, hash-verified observation sidecars beside its native
usage stream. Its timing records distinguish complete attempt wall from actual
settlement wait. A missing-linkage `0.3.2-m8` receipt remains governed by its
matching schema and may carry `suite.pass:null`; `0.3.3-m8` never emits that
state.

# Social-messenger choreography harness

This directory contains the P2-hardened Playwright harness for Clique's
milestone choreography, extended for M8. It launches isolated Alice and Bob
browser contexts, adds Carol for M5 and a second same-account Alice context for
M8, signs them in through the contract's `sm-auth-*` IDs, runs selected `m1()`
through `m6()` and `m8()` segments, and writes structured JSONL receipts.

The harness consumes only test IDs frozen in `../CONTRACT.md`. A runtime guard
rejects any other ID. It never turns missing automation surface into a pass.

## Setup and usage

The instrument intentionally has no lockfile before P3 freeze. A runner must
provision the pinned Playwright and AJV dependencies from `package.json` and the
selected Playwright browser.

```sh
cd benchmarks/tools/social-messenger/choreography
npm install
npx playwright install chromium

CHOREO_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:5173 \
CHOREO_PASSWORD='fixture-password' \
volta run --node 24.18.0 node choreography.mjs m3 \
  --suite-status /absolute/path/suite-status.json
```

`npm test` starts a tiny calibration app, executes M1 and M8 through the real
multi-context harness, validates every emitted receipt against
`receipts.schema.json`, and requires honest segment greens. The app implements
the M8 likes, multi-device unread, live-message, and warm-offline queue surfaces
instead of short-circuiting browser observations. A second M8 run deliberately
serves stale Insights and must exit non-green. The test also exercises the pure
aggregation edge cases: optional skip, required skip, and implemented failure.

The positional segment argument is optional and defaults to `all`. It accepts
`all`, one milestone (`m1` ... `m6` or `m8`), or a comma-separated ordered
subset such as `m1,m3,m8`. `all` runs M1–M6 followed by M8; M7 remains the
brief's separate fresh-session milestone and has no web choreography segment.

Scoring DAG: M3 requires M1 only; M3 does not require M2. Reduced-run
protocol: execute M1, then M2, then M3 in that order. Do not start M3 to
avoid an unfinished M2. A reduced run that skips M2 is non-conforming even
though M3's scoring prerequisite is only M1.

Every implemented CLI flag is:

- `--browser <chromium|firefox|webkit>` — browser engine; default `chromium`.
- `--headed` — show both browser windows; default is headless.
- `--receipts <path>` — JSONL destination; default is `receipts.jsonl` beside
  `choreography.mjs`. The file is truncated at the beginning of each run.
- `--observations <path>` — typed D0.6 assertion-attempt/wait stream; defaults
  to `<receipts>.observations.jsonl`. The metering manifest hash-binds this
  stream before it projects the choreography-owned browser-wait counts. Each
  attempt records only actual locator, predicate, or page-event settlement
  intervals; setup/action and other attempt wall are excluded.
- `--lane-run-id <id>` — required stable lane identity, shared with the
  metering manifest (`CHOREO_LANE_RUN_ID` is the environment form).
- `--suite-status <path>` — required JSON object keyed by milestone. Every
  selected segment must have `{ "pass": boolean, "receipt": string|null }`.
  The runner validates this complete linkage before credentials, Playwright,
  receipt creation, or browser startup. A passing value must carry a non-empty
  suite evidence pointer in `receipt`. Receipt paths are relative to the
  suite-status file, must remain under its directory, and are statted and
  SHA-256 digested before startup. The digest is retained in the segment
  summary so the meter can detect a change when it writes the record.
- `--adapter <path>` — optional lane navigation/fixture adapter. It carries
  route paths and fixture choices only; it cannot report outcomes or bypass
  browser observations. The built-in adapter uses `/profile/{handle}`,
  `/profile/edit`, `/settings`, `/search`, and `/insights` plus the committed
  fixture pack. `routes.insights` may override the M8 Insights route.
- `--simulator-status <path>` — optional separately recorded M6/M8 simulator
  statuses. A single legacy status object is accepted, as is a bundle keyed by
  `m6` and/or `m8`; entries use `{ "id":"ios-simulator-m6"|
  "ios-simulator-m8", "pass":true|false|null, "receipt":string|null,
  "reason":string|null }`. Each entry is retained only in its matching summary
  and never gates web green; see `simulator.md`.
- `--timeout <ms>` — positive integer timeout for ordinary UI observations;
  default `10000`. The M3 2-second appearance and 5-second expiry ceilings are
  fixed by the brief and are not relaxed by this flag.
- `--help` — print usage without loading Playwright.

Exit code `0` means every selected segment has `green:true` (suite plus complete
required choreography). Exit code `1` means execution completed but at least one
segment was not green because a required check was skipped, an implemented
check failed, or suite evidence was absent/failing. Exit code `2` is
configuration or fatal harness failure.

## Environment variables

- `CHOREO_BASE_URL` — required lane web URL.
- `CHOREO_LANE_RUN_ID` — required stable lane identity unless
  `--lane-run-id` is supplied.
- `CHOREO_PASSWORD` — shared fixture password fallback for Alice, Bob, and Carol;
  Alice's M8 second context uses the same Alice credential.
- `CHOREO_ALICE_PASSWORD`, `CHOREO_BOB_PASSWORD` — per-persona passwords;
  `CHOREO_CAROL_PASSWORD` is also required for M5 unless the shared fallback is
  set. Passwords have no CLI flags so
  they do not appear in the process command line.
- `CHOREO_ALICE_EMAIL`, `CHOREO_BOB_EMAIL`, `CHOREO_CAROL_EMAIL` — optional;
  defaults are the corresponding `@example.com` personas from `CONTRACT.md`.
- `CHOREO_BROWSER` — default for `--browser`.
- `CHOREO_RECEIPTS` — default for `--receipts`.
- `CHOREO_OBSERVATIONS` — default for the typed assertion-wait sidecar.
- `CHOREO_SUITE_STATUS` — default for `--suite-status`.
- `CHOREO_ADAPTER` — default for `--adapter`.
- `CHOREO_SIMULATOR_STATUS` — default for `--simulator-status`.
- `CHOREO_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE` — optional browser executable path for runners
  using a system Chromium/Chrome with the Playwright protocol package.
- `CHOREO_TIMEOUT_MS` — default for `--timeout`.

CLI values override their environment defaults. `--headed` has no environment
alias.

## Segment coverage after P2 hardening

Implemented checks make real UI observations and fail normally
when the lane does not satisfy them:

- M1: display-name/bio edits appear on the other client live; session survives
  reload; logout remains signed out across reload.
- M2: live text-post delivery, follow/unfollow Following projection, author
  display name on `sm-feed-item`, live like/unlike count, repost attribution
  and removal, follow-edge vs viewer-repost disambiguation on Following, and
  reply count/thread projection. Live checks run all three trials.
- M3: live DM text on `sm-convo-bubble`, typing visibility within 2 seconds
  and expiry within 5 seconds, plus quoted excerpt and jump behavior through
  the excerpt-only `sm-convo-quote-preview` selector. Live checks run
  best-of-three.
- M4: photo render, video playback, reaction set/replace/remove, edit visibility,
  and delete-for-everyone tombstones across the isolated Alice/Bob contexts.
- M5: group color/background synchronization to Carol, view-once first/second
  view behavior, warm-offline search, and shortened-window disappearing purge.
- M6 web: two offline messages expose pending state, reconnect, arrive exactly
  in order, and reach read receipts.
- M8 web: Bob's like increments Alice's refreshed Insights total; a second
  Alice context receives a same-account message live; opening the conversation
  on Alice client 1 clears `sm-chats-unread` on client 2; and two warm-offline
  Alice clients each queue a message, reconnect in an observed server-arrival
  order, converge without duplicates, and reach normal read receipts.

Remaining unsupported assertions are emitted as `status:"skipped"`, with
`pass:null`, a reason, and whether they are required. Required skips keep the
segment non-green; optional skips are visible but do not masquerade as failures:

- M2 image/video composition (no compose media-picker test ID).
- M2 feed-author avatar (no feed-avatar test ID; display name is required).
- M3 sender-avatar (no sender-avatar test ID; live DM text is required).
- M3 semantic sent/delivered/read tokens (`sm-convo-receipt` exists, but
  glyph/color inference is not an honest state-machine proof).
- M3 group aggregate-receipt and member-removal/history (no group-member
  lifecycle controls in the frozen contract).

The hardening extends the coordination contract for semantic controls and adds
a frozen route/fixture adapter for the four places where navigation cannot be
inferred from a component test ID. The adapter is input-only; the browser still
performs and observes every check.

## Receipts and green aggregation

Each assertion prints one line beginning `STRUCTURED RECEIPT ` and appends the
raw JSON object to the JSONL file. Timing-sensitive assertions always retain all
three attempts. A per-segment summary follows its assertions.

See `receipts-format.md` for field meanings and `receipts.schema.json` for the
machine schema. Milestone green is fail-closed:

```text
green = suite.pass === true && choreography.pass === true
```

Segment summaries also emit `nonGreenCause` (`null` when green; otherwise
`suite-failed` | `choreography-failed` | `required-unimplemented` |
`instrument`). The field remains optional on the schema since `0.3.1-m8` (default
`null`); the emitter always writes it. Prior `0.3.0-m8` receipts remain
governed by their matching schema revision. Lanes MUST copy that field into
the run record. Do not invent a second green label such as "functionally
green".

M6 and M8 web green are intentionally distinct from their simulator artifacts.
`simulator.md` remains the native proof contract; each matching status is
recorded under `choreography.supplementalExternal` and scored as native/O4
evidence rather than silently making web milestones unreachable.

## 0.3.3-m8 migration

`0.3.3-m8` is the coordinated observability bump for LLP 0295 R2. Runners
MUST pass `--suite-status` (or `CHOREO_SUITE_STATUS`) and the file MUST contain
an entry for every selected segment. Missing or partial linkage exits `2`
before any browser or receipt starts; it is no longer represented as a late
`green:false` instrument result. Run records retain the input and suite
receipts in the additive `socialMessenger.suiteStatusLinkage` block.

The same instrument pin adds additive, hash-linked D0.6 milestone fields for
semantic actions, failure-to-recovery episodes, restart/reseed counts, browser
assertion waits, host load, and API interruptions. The run-record extension
stays at version `2` for old-record compatibility; current records must carry
`instrumentVersion: "social-messenger@0.3.3-m8"` and must carry each block as
either claimed or explicitly non-claimed. Browser waits have independent
`suite` and `choreography` owners: this executable claims only choreography,
while the production lane controller records actual suite settlement waits.
The W2 five-counter
native-usage channel is unchanged, while its meter now verifies and joins the
typed observation sidecars.

`0.3.2-m8` uses the unambiguous `sm-convo-quote-preview` selector as the sole
quoted-excerpt jump path after the Clique kit's matching `0.3.1-m8` migration.
`0.3.1-m8` preferred the preview selector with a reply-bubble-scoped legacy
`sm-convo-quote` fallback for `0.3.0`-era clients.
`0.3.0-m8` added the M8 choreography surfaces.
# Social-messenger choreography receipts

Version `0.3.3-m8` writes newline-delimited JSON to `receipts.jsonl`. The same
objects are written to stdout with the literal prefix `STRUCTURED RECEIPT ` so
an outer run harness can separate proof records from ordinary process output.
Each line validates independently against `receipts.schema.json`.

## Assertion receipts

Every browser check emits one `type: "assertion"` object. Its stable identity
is `(segment, assertion)`. The required proof fields are:

- `segment`: one of `m1` through `m6`, or `m8`.
- `assertion`: the stable choreography assertion name.
- `implemented`: whether this harness version actually attempted the check.
- `required`: whether leaving this assertion unimplemented blocks the segment.
- `status`: `passed`, `failed`, or `skipped`.
- `pass`: boolean for an attempted check and `null` for an explicit skip.
- `timings`: every attempt, including errors and all three timing attempts.
- `bestOf`: `1` for ordinary checks and `3` for timing-sensitive checks.

Every timing has both `durationMs` (complete check-attempt wall) and
`settlementWaitMs` (the union of actual locator, predicate, and page-event
wait intervals during that attempt). The latter excludes setup, browser
actions, and computation, and therefore never exceeds `durationMs`. D0.6
choreography wait observations are derived from `settlementWaitMs`, not from
whole-attempt duration. The suite producer records its own settlement waits in
the production lane-controller stream; choreography does not claim them.

An unsupported check is not omitted and never passes. It has
`implemented:false`, `status:"skipped"`, `pass:null`, an empty `timings` array,
and a non-empty `details.reason`. A required skip blocks choreography green; an
optional skip remains visible without being reported as a failed attempt.

For `bestOf:3`, the harness always runs all three attempts. The assertion passes
when at least one attempt passes, and `details.selectedAttempt` identifies the
fastest passing attempt by total `durationMs`; all attempts remain in the
receipt. Metric-specific durations such as `visibleMs` and `expiresMs` remain
under each attempt's `metrics` object. This is best-of-three flake control, not
permission to discard measurements.

For M3's `quoted-reply-excerpt-and-jump` assertion, each attempt's existing
`timing.note` records the `sm-convo-quote-preview` jump selector.

## Segment summaries and milestone green

After the assertion lines, each selected milestone emits one
`type: "segment-summary"` object. This is the per-segment object consumed by the
outer run harness:

```json
{
  "type": "segment-summary",
  "segment": "m3",
  "assertion": "__segment__",
  "implemented": false,
  "required": true,
  "status": "failed",
  "pass": false,
  "timings": [
    {
      "attempt": 1,
      "pass": false,
      "startedAt": null,
      "durationMs": 18234.5,
      "settlementWaitMs": 18001.2,
      "metrics": {}
    }
  ],
  "bestOf": 1,
  "assertions": {
    "total": 3,
    "required": 3,
    "implemented": 2,
    "passed": 2,
    "failed": 0,
    "skipped": 1,
    "notImplemented": 1,
    "requiredUnimplemented": 1
  },
  "suite": { "pass": true, "receipt": "acceptance/m3.json" },
  "choreography": {
    "browserPass": false,
    "requiredExternal": [],
    "externalPass": true,
    "supplementalExternal": [],
    "pass": false
  },
  "green": false,
  "nonGreenCause": "required-unimplemented"
}
```

The normative aggregation is:

1. `browserPass` is true only when every implemented assertion passes and no
   required assertion remains unimplemented. Optional skips therefore stay
   explicit without becoming silent failed attempts.
2. `externalPass` is true when every external leg required for web green passes.
   In `0.3.3-m8` there are no such legs. M6's `ios-simulator-m6` and M8's
   `ios-simulator-m8` statuses are recorded in their matching summaries under
   `supplementalExternal` with `requiredForGreen:false`; they are distinct
   native/O4 artifacts governed by `simulator.md`.
3. `choreography.pass` (and the summary's top-level `pass`) is
   `browserPass && externalPass === true`.
4. `green` is true only when `suite.pass === true && choreography.pass === true`.
   Version `0.3.3-m8` refuses missing or partial suite-status linkage before
   creating receipts or starting a browser, so emitted `suite.pass` is always
   boolean.
5. `nonGreenCause` is the closed recording convention for a non-green
   segment. It is optional on the schema (default `null` when omitted) so
   existing `0.3.0-m8` receipts remain valid; emitters since `0.3.1-m8`
   always write it. Allowed values:
   - `null` — `green` is true. There is no second green label.
   - `required-unimplemented` — a required assertion was skipped.
   - `choreography-failed` — an implemented assertion failed.
   - `suite-failed` — suite evidence is `pass:false`.
   - `instrument` — non-green for an instrument defect other than missing
     suite linkage, which `0.3.3-m8` refuses before startup.

   Lanes MUST copy `nonGreenCause` from this summary into the run record.
   Do not invent labels such as "functionally green". `green` stays a
   boolean; `capability-failure` remains the brief's cap-exhausted
   milestone status, not a synonym for instrument-caused non-green.

The required suite-status input is an object keyed by milestone. Every selected
milestone must be present:

```json
{
  "m1": { "pass": true, "receipt": "acceptance/m1.json" },
  "m2": { "pass": false, "receipt": "acceptance/m2.json" },
  "m8": { "pass": true, "receipt": "acceptance/m8.json" }
}
```

The path is relative to the suite-status file. The choreography does not
interpret or bless the builder's suite semantics, but it does stat and digest
the actual file before startup. The segment summary retains that SHA-256; the
meter re-stats and re-digests the same file at record-write time. A missing or
changed passing receipt refuses rather than becoming green. Coverage-manifest
validation belongs to the outer run harness described by the benchmark brief.

## Compatibility

Consumers must reject an unknown major receipt version and validate with the
schema matching the declared version; unknown fields are rejected. Stable
`(segment, assertion)` names must not be silently repurposed;
changed semantics require a version bump. `nonGreenCause` is an optional
additive field introduced on `0.3.1-m8` segment summaries (default `null`
when omitted); it did not bump the receipt version. `0.3.2-m8` IS a semantic
bump: it removes the legacy `sm-convo-quote` jump fallback, so an M3
`quoted-reply-excerpt-and-jump` receipt at `0.3.2-m8` proves preview-only
selection, while a `0.3.1-m8` receipt may have recorded the reply-bubble-
scoped fallback.

`0.3.3-m8` keeps `0.3.2-m8` selector semantics and makes suite-status linkage
startup-refusing. It coordinates the additive LLP 0295 D0.6 run-record
observability fields without changing `extensionVersion: 2`; the W2 token
meter now joins typed, hash-verified observation sidecars beside its native
usage stream. Its timing records distinguish complete attempt wall from actual
settlement wait. A missing-linkage `0.3.2-m8` receipt remains governed by its
matching schema and may carry `suite.pass:null`; `0.3.3-m8` never emits that
state.

clique-app/app.json clique-app/acceptance.mjs clique-app/App.tsx # Snapback Expo chat starter An Expo (iOS/Android/web) conversation app over a generated Snapback backend: memberships, DM and group inboxes, replies, reactions, image upload via one bound `send` command, and typing presence, in Sessions auth mode. ```sh bun install bun run generate # regenerate after editing snapback/schema.mjs or functions.mjs bun run dev # supervised backend + Expo client bun run prove # the acceptance command (writes .snapback/verify-receipt.json) ``` ## Script glossary `bun run prove`: ordinary completion and the only done-oracle—the authoritative aggregate `snapback verify` receipt (acceptance evidence, not formal proof). `npm test`: raw acceptance implementation that `prove` wraps (debugging). `bun run test:static`: no-server source/generated coherence. `bun run carry:headless`, `bun run carry:web-browser`, `bun run carry:native-simulator`: observation artifacts after accepting the `prove` receipt, never proof authority. `bun run carry:self-check` checks carrier wiring only. Migration: `test:live` was removed; use `npm test` for the same raw acceptance command. ## Extending or ejecting acceptance Keep journey intent and product assertions in `acceptance.mjs`. The public `@expo/snapback-acceptance` package owns server lifecycle, readiness, session minting, bounded retries, cleanup, and starter receipt compatibility; the verify config derives its path registration from the same declaration. Extend the journey with generated-operation path tokens plus `step`, `until`, and `defer`. To replace process management, supply the documented v1 lifecycle adapter; to eject fully, retain the documented v1 receipt contract and let `snapback verify` admit it. The package README is the compatibility contract. Read `AGENTS.md` before adding features — including its security caveat that the client-supplied `senderId` is a seeded-persona demo convenience, not a security boundary. With the dev server running, the served guide and capability index live at `http://127.0.0.1:4287/_snapback/guide/index.md` (or run `snapback guide `). # Building this Snapback app This packet is the whole required first read for this app (LLP 0259 Rung A). Open the edit targets below and work; open one further Guide page only via `snapback guide ` or on a trigger — the brief is outside this packet, a structured `SNAPBACK_*` refusal, or a failed `prove`. ## The loop Edit `snapback/schema.mjs` / `snapback/functions.mjs` / `snapback/seed.json` → `bun run generate` → `bun run dev` (supervises the Expo client; it never launches a device or simulator — Expo Go, a dev client, or `expo run:ios|android` is your job) → `bun run prove`. Before extending or ejecting the proof runner, read `node_modules/@expo/snapback-acceptance/README.md`; it is the supported compatibility and ownership contract. ## Script glossary `bun run prove`: ordinary completion and the only done-oracle—the authoritative aggregate `snapback verify` receipt (acceptance evidence, not formal proof). `npm test`: raw acceptance implementation that `prove` wraps (debugging). `bun run test:static`: no-server source/generated coherence. `bun run carry:headless`, `bun run carry:web-browser`, `bun run carry:native-simulator`: observation artifacts after accepting the `prove` receipt, never proof authority. `bun run carry:self-check` checks carrier wiring only. Migration: `test:live` was removed; use `npm test` for the same raw acceptance command. The native carrier owns simulator boot, drive, and screenshots. Self-started Metro must not inherit `CI=1` (it disables watching); prefer `bun run dev`. ## Edit targets (work files — listed, not charged to the first read) - `snapback/schema.mjs` — sessions auth; user/conversation/membership/message/ reaction tables; ephemeral `typing`. - `snapback/functions.mjs` — inbox and thread live queries, `sendText` / `sendReply` / `react` mutations, and the bound `send` command. - `snapback/seed.json` — seeded demo personas and conversations. - `App.tsx` — generated `app` → `SnapbackExpoProvider`; native retained files; password entry via `useSnapbackCurrentPrincipal` / `useSnapbackAuth`. - `src/screens/inbox-screen.tsx` / `src/screens/chat-screen.tsx` — the `useSnapbackQuery` inbox and `useSurface` thread (replies, reactions, typing, upload) from `@expo/snapback-expo`. - `acceptance.mjs` + `snapback.verify.config.mjs` — the registered proof. `snapback/generated/` is codegen-owned: regenerate, commit `generated/artifacts.json`, never hand-edit outputs. ## Posture - **Auth: sessions mode, guest-first plus ordinary password entry.** The app reaches anonymous `ready`; recovery codes surface once after signup. Supervised dev may provide a guest session for sends and image upload. - **Custody: `volatile-explicit`.** Native durable custody is still pending Phase 2, so this disposable chat template says memory custody explicitly; it does not claim durable native custody or silently weaken a durable policy. Move to `durable-required` only after the native platform row ships. - **Security caveat — client-supplied `senderId` is a demo convenience, never a boundary.** The seeded **TEST PERSONA** control passes the active persona's id as `senderId`/`userId` so demos work. In a real app, derive the sender from the adopted session on the server (`ctx.auth.userId`), drop the argument, and keep personas display-only. ## Safety traps (reconciled at landing) 1. Declare each function's `auth` explicitly in sessions mode: omitting it gets legacy `optional-user` widening plus the `SNAPBACK_AUTH_REQUIREMENT_IMPLICIT` advisory. 2. Inline args objects churn `useSnapbackQuery` — the subscription keys on args identity; hoist or memoize. 3. Structured stored fields (`v.array(...)`, `v.object({...})`) are typed but opaque (experimental): interiors are not queryable, and a nested `v.principal()` is a snapshot, not membership. 4. A changed seed identity never silently resets data: expect `SNAPBACK_SEED_MIGRATION_REQUIRED`, then migrate or reset-install. 5. Every `SNAPBACK_*` refusal names its rule and fix: read it, then run `snapback guide ` for the exact entry. ## Escalate `snapback guide ` returns exact symbols, diagnostic codes, and page anchors — budgeted lookups do not count as extra pages. The [capability index](/_snapback/guide/capabilities.md) is the completeness registry: look up, do not linear-read. Deeper pages, only when triggered: [react-expo clients](/_snapback/guide/clients/react-expo.md), [surfaces](/_snapback/guide/clients/surfaces.md), [sessions and principals](/_snapback/guide/auth/sessions-and-principals.md), [assets](/_snapback/guide/backend/assets.md), [ephemeral state](/_snapback/guide/realtime/ephemeral-state.md). **Stop sign.** Familiar `query()` / `useQuery` is experimental, non-default, and outside this template. If a brief selects it, read the [Familiar handler dialect](/_snapback/guide/backend/familiar-profile.md) before editing. ## Operate it `snapback mcp` serves read-only Guide resources; `snapback mcp-control` adds typed control tools with local admin authority. Preview setup with `snapback agent setup --print --server mcp-control`. With the dev server running this packet is served at `http://127.0.0.1:4287/_snapback/guide/start/expo-chat.md` (replace the origin if startup selected another port); `snapback guide ` is the budgeted lookup channel. inboxes, replies, reactions, image upload via one bound `send` command, and typing presence, in Sessions auth mode. ```sh bun install bun run generate # regenerate after editing snapback/schema.mjs or functions.mjs bun run dev # supervised backend + Expo client bun run prove # the acceptance command (writes .snapback/verify-receipt.json) ``` ## Script glossary `bun run prove`: ordinary completion and the only done-oracle—the authoritative aggregate `snapback verify` receipt (acceptance evidence, not formal proof). `npm test`: raw acceptance implementation that `prove` wraps (debugging). `bun run test:static`: no-server source/generated coherence. `bun run carry:headless`, `bun run carry:web-browser`, `bun run carry:native-simulator`: observation artifacts after accepting the `prove` receipt, never proof authority. `bun run carry:self-check` checks carrier wiring only. Migration: `test:live` was removed; use `npm test` for the same raw acceptance command. ## Extending or ejecting acceptance Keep journey intent and product assertions in `acceptance.mjs`. The public `@expo/snapback-acceptance` package owns server lifecycle, readiness, session minting, bounded retries, cleanup, and starter receipt compatibility; the verify config derives its path registration from the same declaration. Extend the journey with generated-operation path tokens plus `step`, `until`, and `defer`. To replace process management, supply the documented v1 lifecycle adapter; to eject fully, retain the documented v1 receipt contract and let `snapback verify` admit it. The package README is the compatibility contract. Read `AGENTS.md` before adding features — including its security caveat that the client-supplied `senderId` is a seeded-persona demo convenience, not a security boundary. With the dev server running, the served guide and capability index live at `http://127.0.0.1:4287/_snapback/guide/index.md` (or run `snapback guide `). # Building this Snapback app This packet is the whole required first read for this app (LLP 0259 Rung A). Open the edit targets below and work; open one further Guide page only via `snapback guide ` or on a trigger — the brief is outside this packet, a structured `SNAPBACK_*` refusal, or a failed `prove`. ## The loop Edit `snapback/schema.mjs` / `snapback/functions.mjs` / `snapback/seed.json` → `bun run generate` → `bun run dev` (supervises the Expo client; it never launches a device or simulator — Expo Go, a dev client, or `expo run:ios|android` is your job) → `bun run prove`. Before extending or ejecting the proof runner, read `node_modules/@expo/snapback-acceptance/README.md`; it is the supported compatibility and ownership contract. ## Script glossary `bun run prove`: ordinary completion and the only done-oracle—the authoritative aggregate `snapback verify` receipt (acceptance evidence, not formal proof). `npm test`: raw acceptance implementation that `prove` wraps (debugging). `bun run test:static`: no-server source/generated coherence. `bun run carry:headless`, `bun run carry:web-browser`, `bun run carry:native-simulator`: observation artifacts after accepting the `prove` receipt, never proof authority. `bun run carry:self-check` checks carrier wiring only. Migration: `test:live` was removed; use `npm test` for the same raw acceptance command. The native carrier owns simulator boot, drive, and screenshots. Self-started Metro must not inherit `CI=1` (it disables watching); prefer `bun run dev`. ## Edit targets (work files — listed, not charged to the first read) - `snapback/schema.mjs` — sessions auth; user/conversation/membership/message/ reaction tables; ephemeral `typing`. - `snapback/functions.mjs` — inbox and thread live queries, `sendText` / `sendReply` / `react` mutations, and the bound `send` command. - `snapback/seed.json` — seeded demo personas and conversations. - `App.tsx` — generated `app` → `SnapbackExpoProvider`; native retained files; password entry via `useSnapbackCurrentPrincipal` / `useSnapbackAuth`. - `src/screens/inbox-screen.tsx` / `src/screens/chat-screen.tsx` — the `useSnapbackQuery` inbox and `useSurface` thread (replies, reactions, typing, upload) from `@expo/snapback-expo`. - `acceptance.mjs` + `snapback.verify.config.mjs` — the registered proof. `snapback/generated/` is codegen-owned: regenerate, commit `generated/artifacts.json`, never hand-edit outputs. ## Posture - **Auth: sessions mode, guest-first plus ordinary password entry.** The app reaches anonymous `ready`; recovery codes surface once after signup. Supervised dev may provide a guest session for sends and image upload. - **Custody: `volatile-explicit`.** Native durable custody is still pending Phase 2, so this disposable chat template says memory custody explicitly; it does not claim durable native custody or silently weaken a durable policy. Move to `durable-required` only after the native platform row ships. - **Security caveat — client-supplied `senderId` is a demo convenience, never a boundary.** The seeded **TEST PERSONA** control passes the active persona's id as `senderId`/`userId` so demos work. In a real app, derive the sender from the adopted session on the server (`ctx.auth.userId`), drop the argument, and keep personas display-only. ## Safety traps (reconciled at landing) 1. Declare each function's `auth` explicitly in sessions mode: omitting it gets legacy `optional-user` widening plus the `SNAPBACK_AUTH_REQUIREMENT_IMPLICIT` advisory. 2. Inline args objects churn `useSnapbackQuery` — the subscription keys on args identity; hoist or memoize. 3. Structured stored fields (`v.array(...)`, `v.object({...})`) are typed but opaque (experimental): interiors are not queryable, and a nested `v.principal()` is a snapshot, not membership. 4. A changed seed identity never silently resets data: expect `SNAPBACK_SEED_MIGRATION_REQUIRED`, then migrate or reset-install. 5. Every `SNAPBACK_*` refusal names its rule and fix: read it, then run `snapback guide ` for the exact entry. ## Escalate `snapback guide ` returns exact symbols, diagnostic codes, and page anchors — budgeted lookups do not count as extra pages. The [capability index](/_snapback/guide/capabilities.md) is the completeness registry: look up, do not linear-read. Deeper pages, only when triggered: [react-expo clients](/_snapback/guide/clients/react-expo.md), [surfaces](/_snapback/guide/clients/surfaces.md), [sessions and principals](/_snapback/guide/auth/sessions-and-principals.md), [assets](/_snapback/guide/backend/assets.md), [ephemeral state](/_snapback/guide/realtime/ephemeral-state.md). **Stop sign.** Familiar `query()` / `useQuery` is experimental, non-default, and outside this template. If a brief selects it, read the [Familiar handler dialect](/_snapback/guide/backend/familiar-profile.md) before editing. ## Operate it `snapback mcp` serves read-only Guide resources; `snapback mcp-control` adds typed control tools with local admin authority. Preview setup with `snapback agent setup --print --server mcp-control`. With the dev server running this packet is served at `http://127.0.0.1:4287/_snapback/guide/start/expo-chat.md` (replace the origin if startup selected another port); `snapback guide ` is the budgeted lookup channel. functions.mjs bun run dev # supervised backend + Expo client bun run prove # the acceptance command (writes .snapback/verify-receipt.json) ``` ## Script glossary `bun run prove`: ordinary completion and the only done-oracle—the authoritative aggregate `snapback verify` receipt (acceptance evidence, not formal proof). `npm test`: raw acceptance implementation that `prove` wraps (debugging). `bun run test:static`: no-server source/generated coherence. `bun run carry:headless`, `bun run carry:web-browser`, `bun run carry:native-simulator`: observation artifacts after accepting the `prove` receipt, never proof authority. `bun run carry:self-check` checks carrier wiring only. Migration: `test:live` was removed; use `npm test` for the same raw acceptance command. ## Extending or ejecting acceptance Keep journey intent and product assertions in `acceptance.mjs`. The public `@expo/snapback-acceptance` package owns server lifecycle, readiness, session minting, bounded retries, cleanup, and starter receipt compatibility; the verify config derives its path registration from the same declaration. Extend the journey with generated-operation path tokens plus `step`, `until`, and `defer`. To replace process management, supply the documented v1 lifecycle adapter; to eject fully, retain the documented v1 receipt contract and let `snapback verify` admit it. The package README is the compatibility contract. Read `AGENTS.md` before adding features — including its security caveat that the client-supplied `senderId` is a seeded-persona demo convenience, not a security boundary. Self-started Metro must not inherit `CI=1` (it disables watching); prefer `bun run dev`. ## Edit targets (work files — listed, not charged to the first read) - `snapback/schema.mjs` — sessions auth; user/conversation/membership/message/ reaction tables; ephemeral `typing`. - `snapback/functions.mjs` — inbox and thread live queries, `sendText` / `sendReply` / `react` mutations, and the bound `send` command. - `snapback/seed.json` — seeded demo personas and conversations. - `App.tsx` — generated `app` → `SnapbackExpoProvider`; native retained files; password entry via `useSnapbackCurrentPrincipal` / `useSnapbackAuth`. - `src/screens/inbox-screen.tsx` / `src/screens/chat-screen.tsx` — the `useSnapbackQuery` inbox and `useSurface` thread (replies, reactions, typing, upload) from `@expo/snapback-expo`. - `acceptance.mjs` + `snapback.verify.config.mjs` — the registered proof. `snapback/generated/` is codegen-owned: regenerate, commit `generated/artifacts.json`, never hand-edit outputs. ## Posture - **Auth: sessions mode, guest-first plus ordinary password entry.** The app reaches anonymous `ready`; recovery codes surface once after signup. Move to `durable-required` only after the native platform row ships. - **Security caveat — client-supplied `senderId` is a demo convenience, never a boundary.** The seeded **TEST PERSONA** control passes the active persona's id as `senderId`/`userId` so demos work. Declare each function's `auth` explicitly in sessions mode: omitting it gets legacy `optional-user` widening plus the `SNAPBACK_AUTH_REQUIREMENT_IMPLICIT` advisory. 2. Inline args objects churn `useSnapbackQuery` — the subscription keys on args identity; hoist or memoize. 3. Structured stored fields (`v.array(...)`, `v.object({...})`) are typed but opaque (experimental): interiors are not queryable, and a nested `v.principal()` is a snapshot, not membership. 4. # Bind a principal to your app's user identity

> **Local target only.** This page describes the local dev/test target.
> Hosted targets make deliberately weaker or different claims — see
> [auth/targets](./targets.md).

Almost every app ported onto Snapback already has its own user identity: a
`users` table with a `sourceUserID` from an OAuth provider, roles, a display
name, rows that point at it. Snapback gives you a different thing —
`ctx.auth.userId`, a **server-minted principal id**. Making an existing app
work means building the join between them: a principal↔app-user table, and a
trustworthy way to populate it.

This page is that recipe. It is the first thing a port needs and the easiest
thing to get wrong, because the obvious approach — a mutation that takes the
app's user id as an argument and binds it to the caller's principal — is a
complete authentication bypass.

## Claims can inform behavior; they cannot populate a binding yet

A real catalog-backed session now exposes a deeply frozen
`ctx.auth.claims`. It contains only the identity that authenticated this
session plus active, applicable assurance records. Email, phone, and username
use their catalog-canonical value; OIDC and other federated identities expose
their exact provider/issuer/subject and omit mutable profile values. Anonymous,
dev-impersonated, admin, system, and agent authority do not receive claims.

This makes read-only in-handler inspection possible, but does not make an
ordinary `bindMe(...)` mutation safe. Snapback does not yet invoke the sealed
verified-provisioning writer described by LLP 0214 §§5.3–5.5. A
`verifiedProvisioning` identity-binding declaration currently installs the
write seal only: ordinary buffered writes and every HostPlan/IR write form fail
with `SNAPBACK_AUTH_BINDING_WRITE_FORBIDDEN`. Codegen also rejects the sealed
table as a declared handler, generated data-resource/data-transaction write
target, maintained-projection output, or non-empty versioned-seed target. Runtime
rechecks buffered batches, HostPlan writes, declarative seed installation, and
both projection rebuild and same-transaction maintenance. Schema migration and
destructive reset remain separately authorized operator lifecycle operations;
neither is an application binding writer.

> **The future sealed writer may use claims to select the app row once. The
> durable binding key will still be `ctx.auth.userId`.** Email is mutable, and
> an issuer/subject pair belongs to the auth substrate; neither replaces the
> principal in steady-state app reads or writes.

Never accept a claims object, email, subject, or app-user id from the client as
proof. Those are selection inputs under caller control.

## Define the binding table

Whichever way you populate it, the table itself is the same shape: one row
per principal, uniquely indexed on **every** side so the mapping cannot fan
out. The Zerobugs control's declaration:

```js source=demos/zerobugs/control/snapback/schema.mjs
export const identityBinding = defineTable({
  principal: v.principal(),
  userID: v.id('user'),
  sourceUserID: v.string(),
})
  .index('by_principal', ['principal'], { unique: true })
  .index('by_user', ['userID'], { unique: true })
  .index('by_source_user_id', ['sourceUserID'], { unique: true });
```

Three unique indexes, not one. `by_principal` stops a principal owning two
app identities; `by_user` and `by_source_user_id` stop one app identity being
claimed by two principals. The storage constraint is the backstop that
survives a bug in the handler logic — see
[declare structural uniqueness](../backend/mutations.md#declare-structural-uniqueness).

Keep the physical reference (`v.id('user')`) *and* the external id
(`sourceUserID`) as separate fields: the typed id is what private rows join
on, and the external string is what a provider lookup or an audit trail needs.

Do not declare this table under `verifiedProvisioning` and then try to write it
from an application handler: the declaration seals the table, but there is no
host-invoked inside writer yet. Until that platform lane lands, use Pattern A
or the acceptance-only Pattern B below on an undeclared table, with their
trusted-writer and reachability constraints intact.

After creation, every protected handler resolves only
`principal → binding → app row`; it does not repeat a claim lookup.

## Resolve the principal in every protected handler

Once the row exists, no handler ever accepts a caller-supplied identity again.
Every private read and write starts by resolving principal → binding → app
row, and re-verifies the binding still names the same row it did at write
time:

```js source=demos/zerobugs/control/snapback/functions.mjs
export async function requireSourceUser(ctx) {
  requireFixtureSession(ctx);
  const principal = ctx.auth.userId;
  const binding = await ctx.db
    .query('identityBinding')
    .withIndex('by_principal')
    .eq('principal', principal)
    .first();
  if (!binding) {
    throw new Error('session principal is not bound to a source user');
  }
  const user = await ctx.db.get('user', binding.userID);
  if (
    !user
    || user.id !== binding.sourceUserID
    || (user.role !== 'crew' && user.role !== 'user')
  ) {
    throw new Error('session principal has an invalid source user binding');
  }
  return user;
}
```

(`requireFixtureSession(ctx)` is the Zerobugs control's own fixture gate — it
just refuses an unauthenticated `ctx` before fixture work; your port omits it
and relies on `auth: 'authenticated'` plus the binding resolution below.)

Roles come from the resolved app row, never from a mint argument or a request
body:

```js source=demos/zerobugs/control/snapback/functions.mjs
export async function requireCrew(ctx) {
  const user = await requireSourceUser(ctx);
  if (user.role !== 'crew') {
    throw new Error('source user is not authorized');
  }
  return user;
}
```

Expose the caller's own binding as a query taking **no arguments** — the
absence of an identity selector is the point, and it is worth asserting in a
test that the generated args schema is empty:

```js source=demos/zerobugs/control/snapback/functions.mjs
export const acceptanceActorBindingSelf = defineJsQuery({
  auth: 'authenticated',
  args: {},
  reads: ['identityBinding', 'user'],
  result: results.records(v.object({
    principal: v.string(),
    sourceUserID: v.string(),
    userID: v.id('user'),
    role: v.string(),
  })),
  handler: async (ctx) => {
    const user = await requireSourceUser(ctx);
    return [{
      principal: ctx.auth.userId,
      sourceUserID: user.id,
      userID: user._id,
      role: user.role,
    }];
  },
});
```

If your app also uses [scoped roles](./scoped-roles.md) or `authScopeField`
query scoping, those compare against the **principal**, not the app user row.
Store the principal on rows you want scoped by the declarative surface, and
use the binding for everything that must reach the app's own user record.

## Pattern A — still conforming: bind in trusted server code

This is the strongest executable shape today, not a hosted-production claim.
Snapback's local external-identity seam uses a trusted server-side component
that authenticates the user through your existing front door
(OAuth, your own login), calls the `auth.mintSession` host operation for that
verified identity, and hands the resulting bearer back to that same user.

The broker is the only place that holds all three facts at once — the
verified external identity, the app user row it maps to, and the principal
`auth.mintSession` just returned. So the broker is where the binding row gets
written, before the bearer is released:

This pattern currently uses an ordinary, deliberately non-public mutation, so
its binding table must not be declared as a `verifiedProvisioning`
identity-binding table. That declaration would correctly seal the write.

```js fragment reason="broker-side shape; the mint host-op authorities and the adopt-bearer half are the subject of auth/native-apps.md"
// Trusted server-side broker (never in an app bundle):
const verified = await myIdentityProvider.verify(request);      // your front door
const appUser = await myUsers.findBySubject(verified.subject);  // your user row
const minted = await hostOps.auth.mintSession({ email: verified.email });
const session = createExternalSessionClient(baseUrl, { bearerToken: minted.token });

// Only now — knowing both sides — write the binding under privileged authority,
// then release the bearer to this user and nobody else.
await session.mutate(api.bindVerifiedIdentity, {
  args: { issuer: verified.issuer, subject: verified.subject },
});
return { bearerToken: minted.token };
```

Two properties make this safe, and both are load-bearing:

- **The binding mutation is privileged, not public.** It is invoked with the
  broker's authority, is idempotent per principal, and refuses a principal or
  app user that is already bound. It must not be reachable from an ordinary
  client session; if your app has a public gateway or function allowlist,
  leave it out of the allowlist (see the omission technique below).
- **The bearer is released only to the authenticated caller.** A generic
  "mint a session for this email" endpoint with no front door is the same
  bypass in a different place.

The client then adopts the bearer with
`createExternalSessionClient(baseUrl, { bearerToken })` and carries it
normally; rotation goes through `replaceBearerToken`. Both halves are covered
in [authenticate a native app](./native-apps.md).

For a browser that needs durable coordinator custody, do not stop at that
external-bearer client. The registered
[browser sign-in and reload recipe](../recipes/browser-auth.md) stages a
one-use challenge/code and lets ordinary `authExchange` move the bearer into
`AuthCoordinator`'s IndexedDB record. It proves the private binder's gateway
omission, full-page restoration without another exchange, logout revocation,
and cross-subject protected-data isolation in real Chrome.

**Honest boundary:** `auth.mintSession` is a dev/test/demo host operation
requiring the admin token, the process-bound impersonation capability, and
active sessions mode. From a terminal, the paved spelling of the same
operation is `snapback session mint --email <email> --ready-file <ready-file>`.
LLP 0045's production email delivery adapter is unbuilt
and the Cloudflare arm exposes no sessions routes, so this page does not claim
hosted production identity. The *pattern* is the production shape; the
current mint mechanism is local.

## Pattern B — acceptance harness: a frozen actor map

An acceptance suite has a different problem. It needs several real principals
bound to specific fixture users so it can assert per-actor visibility, and
principal ids are freshly minted every run — so nothing can be seeded. But the
suite also has something a product does not: a **frozen fixture**, whose exact
user population is known in advance.

The Zerobugs control uses that to build a bootstrap that is safe *because*
it is closed. Five properties, all of them necessary:

1. **A frozen actor map.** The mutation's argument is an actor *name* from a
   closed set (`'creator'`, `'crew-admin'`, …), not a source user id. It
   selects one member of a hard-coded map; anything else refuses.
2. **A complete-fixture precondition.** Binding refuses unless exactly the
   frozen fixture is loaded — the right user count, the right ids, the right
   roles, the completion sentinel present.
3. **One-to-one refusal on both sides.**
4. **Set closure.** After the last actor is bound, the mutation refuses
   permanently.
5. **Gateway omission.** The bootstrap operations are absent from the app's
   function allowlist, so they are reachable only over the direct client the
   harness drives — never over the product's HTTP surface.

```js source=demos/zerobugs/control/snapback/functions.mjs
    const principal = ctx.auth.userId;
    const existingPrincipal = await ctx.db
      .query('identityBinding')
      .withIndex('by_principal')
      .eq('principal', principal)
      .first();
    if (existingPrincipal) {
      throw new Error('session principal is already bound');
    }

    const existingBindings = await ctx.db.query('identityBinding').take(6).collect();
    if (existingBindings.length >= 5) {
      throw new Error('actor binding is closed after the frozen actor set is complete');
    }

    const [existingUser, existingSource] = await Promise.all([
      ctx.db
        .query('identityBinding')
        .withIndex('by_user')
        .eq('userID', sourceUser._id)
        .first(),
      ctx.db
        .query('identityBinding')
        .withIndex('by_source_user_id')
        .eq('sourceUserID', sourceUser.id)
        .first(),
    ]);
    if (existingUser || existingSource) {
      throw new Error('source user is already bound');
    }
```

The suite drives it by minting one session per actor (see
[mint test personas](./sessions-and-principals.md#mint-test-personas-the-complete-local-recipe)),
calling the binding mutation once per persona, and then proving the mapping
by reading `acceptanceActorBindingSelf` back. A rerun against an
already-bound instance must observe the refusal and then prove the existing
row is the same one-to-one mapping — that is what makes the harness idempotent
without weakening the refusal.

The same closure technique gates the fixture loader itself; see
[loading large deterministic fixtures](../testing/large-fixtures.md#gate-the-loader-in-a-sessions-app).

**This is a harness pattern, not a product answer.** Its safety comes
entirely from the frozen fixture and the closed actor set. Do not lift it
into an application: without those, the actor argument is a caller-selected
identity again.

**Evidence:** the control's binding surface is exercised by its own
`bun run test:lane2` (runtime-independent witnesses) and `test:lane2:live`
(a seven-actor live gate), and by the retained ZB gate receipts under
[`demos/zerobugs/evidence`](repo:demos/zerobugs/evidence). It is not part of
the repository's CI proof; treat the snippets as a reviewed reference
implementation whose behavior is receipt-witnessed at a point in time.

## Reset reissues principals; it does not reissue app rows

`app.reset` advances the auth boundary: existing bearers stop working and the
same email remints to a **different** `userId`
([reset invalidates sessions](./sessions-and-principals.md#reset-invalidates-sessions-and-reissues-principals)).
Your app user rows, if they are seeded, survive. So every binding row is stale
after a reset and must be rebuilt.

Two rules follow:

- **Never seed a binding row with a captured principal id.** Seed the app
  users; bind after the reset, once real principals exist.
- **Order the bootstrap: reset → load fixture → mint principals → bind.**
  The dependency is circular by nature (the fixture creates the users a later
  binding maps to), which is exactly why the loader and the binder each carry
  their own closure sentinel.

## Current boundary

The local target now supplies verified read-only claims and a complete
ordinary-write seal for declared identity-binding tables. It does **not** yet
supply the host-invoked writer inside that seal. Pattern A and the frozen
Pattern B remain the executable conforming choices because they arrange for a
trusted writer to hold both sides before releasing or using the principal;
their tables remain undeclared until the host writer exists. Draft LLP 0151
separately owns future provider identity/lifecycle and hosted-target work; this
app-level join does not pretend to implement it.

## Anti-patterns

- **Do not accept an app user id as a mutation argument and bind it to the
  caller's principal.** That is the bypass this whole page exists to prevent;
  the caller controls the argument.
- **Do not write a `verifiedProvisioning` handler today.** Its declared
  identity-binding table is sealed against ordinary handlers, and the
  host-invoked inside writer remains an open platform ask.
- **Do not derive the app identity from anything the client sends** — not an
  email in the body, not a header, not a JWT the client hands you. If the
  handler did not mint it, the handler cannot verify it.
- **Do not index only `by_principal`.** Without unique indexes on the app-user
  and external-id sides, one app identity can be bound by two principals.
- **Do not seed binding rows.** Principal ids are minted per run and reissued
  by reset; a seeded binding points at an identity that no longer exists.
- **Do not leave the bootstrap binding mutation in your public function
  allowlist.** Reachability from an ordinary client session turns a closed
  bootstrap back into an identity-selection API.
- **Do not read app roles from the session.** Resolve the binding and read
  the role off the app row.

# Bind a principal to your app's user identity

> **Local target only.** This page describes the local dev/test target.
> Hosted targets make deliberately weaker or different claims — see
> [auth/targets](./targets.md).

Almost every app ported onto Snapback already has its own user identity: a
`users` table with a `sourceUserID` from an OAuth provider, roles, a display
name, rows that point at it. Snapback gives you a different thing —
`ctx.auth.userId`, a **server-minted principal id**. Making an existing app
work means building the join between them: a principal↔app-user table, and a
trustworthy way to populate it.

This page is that recipe. It is the first thing a port needs and the easiest
thing to get wrong, because the obvious approach — a mutation that takes the
app's user id as an argument and binds it to the caller's principal — is a
complete authentication bypass.

## Claims can inform behavior; they cannot populate a binding yet

A real catalog-backed session now exposes a deeply frozen
`ctx.auth.claims`. It contains only the identity that authenticated this
session plus active, applicable assurance records. Email, phone, and username
use their catalog-canonical value; OIDC and other federated identities expose
their exact provider/issuer/subject and omit mutable profile values. Anonymous,
dev-impersonated, admin, system, and agent authority do not receive claims.

This makes read-only in-handler inspection possible, but does not make an
ordinary `bindMe(...)` mutation safe. Snapback does not yet invoke the sealed
verified-provisioning writer described by LLP 0214 §§5.3–5.5. A
`verifiedProvisioning` identity-binding declaration currently installs the
write seal only: ordinary buffered writes and every HostPlan/IR write form fail
with `SNAPBACK_AUTH_BINDING_WRITE_FORBIDDEN`. Codegen also rejects the sealed
table as a declared handler, generated data-resource/data-transaction write
target, maintained-projection output, or non-empty versioned-seed target. Runtime
rechecks buffered batches, HostPlan writes, declarative seed installation, and
both projection rebuild and same-transaction maintenance. Schema migration and
destructive reset remain separately authorized operator lifecycle operations;
neither is an application binding writer.

> **The future sealed writer may use claims to select the app row once. The
> durable binding key will still be `ctx.auth.userId`.** Email is mutable, and
> an issuer/subject pair belongs to the auth substrate; neither replaces the
> principal in steady-state app reads or writes.

Never accept a claims object, email, subject, or app-user id from the client as
proof. Those are selection inputs under caller control.

Whichever way you populate it, the table itself is the same shape: one row
per principal, uniquely indexed on **every** side so the mapping cannot fan
out. The Zerobugs control's declaration:

```js source=demos/zerobugs/control/snapback/schema.mjs
export const identityBinding = defineTable({
  principal: v.principal(),
  userID: v.id('user'),
  sourceUserID: v.string(),

  .index('by_principal', ['principal'], { unique: true })
  .index('by_user', ['userID'], { unique: true })
  .index('by_source_user_id', ['sourceUserID'], { unique: true });

claimed by two principals. The storage constraint is the backstop that
survives a bug in the handler logic — see
[declare structural uniqueness](../backend/mutations.md#declare-structural-uniqueness).
